Description
100 Gram PAMP Suisse Gold Bar – Lady Fortuna is manufactured by the world’s leading independent precious metal refiner
PAMP Suisse
,
which has some of the highest standards (and one of the most impressive facilities in the world) for transparency and authenticity in the entire gold industry.
They’ve held that distinction for over 35 years, having started producing some of the world’s finest bars and ingots as early as 1977.
PAMP Suisse Lady Fortuna Gold is one of the world’s most popular gold bars.
The PAMP Suisse is popular gold bar series among investors because of its low margin over the spot, beautiful design, and reputation worldwide. Investing in a 100 Gram Gold Bar has credentials to be an effective method of shielding investments from inflation throughout history.
One of the top-notch qualities of this 100g PAMP Suisse Gold Bar is that it features world-beating Veriscan technology. If you’re not sure what Veriscan technology is, no worries, it’s basically a serialization technology that ensures each of the 9’s printed on the front aren’t just for show. By giving open access to the Veriscan database, customers themselves are able to verify the authenticity of these bars.
Design of Pamp Suisse 100 Gram Gold Bar – Lady Fortuna
The design of Pamp Suisse 100 Gram Gold Bar – Lady Fortuna is one of the more stunning to ever find its way onto an ingot, and the entire world is taking a preferential attitude towards its appearance.
The Pamp Suisse Gold Bar 100g features the depiction of the left-profile bust of Lady Fortuna on the obverse. Lady Fortuna is a Roman Goddess associated with fortune, luck, virtue, and chance. Lady Fortuna along with a wheel slightly visible behind her left profile figure, which is blindfolded, and a cornucopia atop of her head is depicted.
On the reverse side of 100g gold bar – PAMP Suisse Lady Fortuna features the depiction of the PAMP Suisse logo, weight, purity, metal content, a unique serial number on the reverse & the Roman Goddess of prosperity and welfare which also well-known as the protector of grain supplies. Inscriptions are arranged vertically down toward the face of the 100 gram gold bar Pamp Suisse.
